prs.head: 8686ca9726be9f617f0ea790bbf3d3ea8fd2c0c2
prs.body:
### Description

SLi-Rec's masked attention constructs the TensorFlow-era sentinel `-(2**32)+1` in the score dtype. It cannot be represented in float16, so `full_like` raises before masking even for an entirely valid history. A complete SLi-Rec forward pass under CPU float16 autocast also fails.

Bound this finite sentinel by the score dtype's minimum finite value. Float32, float64 and bfloat16 retain the existing sentinel; float16 uses its representable lower bound. The existing fully padded-row behavior remains finite and unchanged.

Fixes #2450.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43896904939) checks exact head `8686ca9726be9f617f0ea790bbf3d3ea8fd2c0c2` against unchanged staging:

- Python 3.10 and 3.11 with PyTorch 2.5.1: unchanged model suite **12 passed**; new cases on the baseline **4 failed, 10 passing controls**; patched model suite **26 passed**.
- Python 3.10 with the declared PyTorch 2.0.1 minimum: **22 passed, 4 skipped**. Independent tiny operator probes confirm that this version lacks the CPU half linear/autocast support required by those four cases. Supported dtype cases run normally.
- Tests cover float16/bfloat16/float32/float64 with empty, partial and full masks, plus complete SLi-Rec autocast forward, backward and optimizer steps.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 reproduces the same four failures and passes all 26 patched tests.

### History review

Checked 1,497 upstream PR heads, 69 existing fork branches and all 15 reachable SLi-Rec source versions, including previous TensorFlow paths, the former `sli_rec_pytorch.py` filename and intermediate commits. This fix is limited to attention sentinel representability.

### Checklist

- [x] Contribution guidelines and code style followed.
- [x] Regression tests added to the existing registered model test module.
- [x] Comments explain the numerical choice; public API is unchanged.
- [x] Commits include the required `Signed-off-by` trailer.
- [x] Targets `staging`.

prs.head: a9147aa957d9793832899e1285febfe95eae77a0
prs.body:
### Description

The adaptive preference-fusion gate reads `time_to_now[:, -1:]`, but the dataset left-aligns history and pads the remaining columns. Short histories therefore supply a padded zero instead of the interval since the latest real behavior. With two observations and a three-day gap, the gate receives `log(3)` at maximum length 2 and zero at maximum length 5.

Use the existing sequence length to gather the last observed time, and supply a neutral zero for an empty history. Full and truncated histories keep their existing temporal context. The correction changes the fusion feature only; checkpoint parameter shapes are unchanged.

Fixes #2456.

### Validation

[Independent validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/recommenders/actions/runs/43896904939) checks exact head `a9147aa957d9793832899e1285febfe95eae77a0` on Python 3.10/PyTorch 2.0.1 and Python 3.10–3.11/PyTorch 2.5.1:

- Unchanged SLi-Rec suite: **12 passed**.
- New cases on the baseline: **7 failed, 8 passing controls**.
- Patched model suite: **27 passed**.
- Native dataset tests cover short/full/truncated histories, maximum length one, and positive/negative sample groups. Additional cases cover mixed and empty masks and noncontiguous time tensors.
- Complete float32/float64 model predictions, parameter gradients and Adam updates match a separate row-wise reference that selects the last observed event.
- Black and `git diff --check` pass. Local Python 3.12.14/PyTorch 2.5.1 gives the same results.

### References and history

The [SLi-Rec paper, section 3.3](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2019/0585.pdf) uses temporal context to adapt preference fusion and evaluates the interval since a user's last behavior. This patch restores the observed interval as the fusion input.

Checked 1,497 upstream PR heads, 69 existing fork branches and all 15 reachable SLi-Rec source versions, including former TensorFlow paths, the former `sli_rec_pytorch.py` filename and intermediate commits. All historical variants select the final padded column.

### Checklist

- [x] Contribution guidelines and code style followed.
- [x] Regression tests added to the existing registered model test module.
- [x] The code comment explains the padding/recency distinction.
- [x] Commit includes the required `Signed-off-by` trailer.
- [x] Targets `staging`.
